literal: If she sees those who sit idle, saying 'we have nothing' and being lazy, the good lady called Earth will laugh.
translation: If the good lady called Earth sees those who sit idle, lazily complaining 'we have nothing,' she will laugh in mockery.
modern: "எங்களிடம் ஏதும் இல்லை" என்று சோம்பேறியாக அமர்ந்திருப்பவர்களைக் கண்டால், பூமிதேவி என்னும் நல்லவள் பார்த்துச் சிரிப்பாள்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the value of agricultural labor and the absurdity of complaining about poverty while refusing to work the land. The poet personifies the Earth as a 'good lady' (நல்லாள்) who is ready to yield wealth to those who toil. When people sit idle, lazily complaining that they have nothing, the Earth laughs at their foolishness because the source of abundance is right beneath their feet, waiting to be cultivated. The word 'அசைஇ' denotes being lazy or inactive, and 'நகும்' indicates her mocking laughter at their self-imposed poverty.
